edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), Scorpiace adversus Gnosticos, via Latin Wikisource transcription

source_text: Magnum de modico malum scorpios terra suppurat: tot venena, quot genera; tot pernicies, quot et species; tot dolores, quot et colores, Nicander scribit et pingit: et tamen unus omnium violentiae gestus nocere de cauda; quae cauda erit, quodcumque de postumo corporis propagatur, et verberat. Proinde scorpii series illa nodorum, venenata intrinsecus venula subtilis, arcuato impetu surgens, hamatile spiculum in summo tormenti ratione stringit; unde et bellicam machinam, retractu tela vegetantem, de scorpio nominant. Id spiculum, et fistula est, patula tenuitate in vulnus et virus, qua figit effundit. Familiare periculi tempus aestas; Austro et Africo saevitia velificat. In remediis naturalia plurima; aliquid et magia circumligat, medicina cum ferro et poculo occurrit. Nam et praebibunt quidam, festinando tutelam; sed concubitus exhaurit, et denuo sitiunt. Nobis fides praesidium, si non et ipsa percutitur diffidentia signandi statim et adjurandi, et urgendi bestiae calcem: hoc denique modo etiam ethnicis saepe subvenimus; donati a Deo ea potestate, quam Apostolus dedicavit, cum morsum viperae sprevit. Quid ergo promittit stylus iste, si fides de suo tuta est? Ut et alias de suo tuta sit, cum suos scorpios patitur. Acerba mediocritas et istis, et genus varium, et uno modo armantur, et certo tempore subornantur, nec alio quam ardoris. Hoc apud Christianos persecutio est. Cum igitur fides aestuat, et Ecclesia exuritur de figura rubi, tunc Gnostici erumpunt, tunc Valentiniani proserpunt, tunc omnes martyriorum refragatores ebulliunt, calentes et ipsi offendere, figere, occidere. Nam quod sciant multos simplices ac rudes, tum infirmos, plerosque vero in ventum, et si placuerit, christianos, nunquam magis adeundos sapiunt, quam cum aditus animae formido laxavit; praesertim cum aliqua atrocitas fidem martyrum coronavit. Itaque primo trahentes adhuc caudam de affectibus applicant, aut quasi in vacuum flagellant. Haeccine pati homines innocentes? ut putes fratrem, aut de melioribus ethnicum? Siccine tractari sectam nemini molestam? Dehinc adigunt, perire homines sine caussa. Perire enim, et sine caussa, prima fixura. Exinde jam caedunt. Sed nesciunt simplices animae, quid, quomodo scriptum sit, ubi, et quando, et coram quibus confitendum, nisi quod nec simplicitas ista, sed vanitas, imo dementia, pro Deo mori. Et: Quis me salvum faciat, si is occidet, qui salvum facere debebit? Semel Christus pro nobis obiit, semel occisus est ne occideremur. Si vicem repetit, nunc et ille salutem de mea nece exspectat? An Deus hominum mundi sanguinem flagitat, maxime si taurorum et hircorum recusat? Certe peccatoris poenitentiam mavult quam mortem. Et quomodo non peccatorum desiderat mortem? Haec, et si qua alia admenta haereticorum venenorum, quem non vel in scrupulum figant, si non in exitium? vel in bilem, si non in mortem? At tu, fides si vigilat, ibidem scorpio pro solea anathema illidito, et relinquito in suo sopore morientem. Caeterum, si plagam satiaverit, intimat virus, et properat in viscera; statim omnes pristini sensus retorpescunt, sanguis animi gelascit, carne spiritus exolescit, nausea nominis inaccrescit. Jam et ipsa mens sibi quo vomat quaerit. Atque ita semel infirmitas quae percussa est, sauciatam fidem vel in haeresim, vel in saeculum exspirat. Et nunc praesentia rerum est medius ardor ipsa canicula persecutionis: ab ipso scilicet cynocephalo. Alios ignis, alios gladius, alios bestiae Christianos probaverunt. Alii fustibus interim et ungulis insuper degustata martyria in carcere esuriunt. Nos ipsi ut lepores, destinata venatio, de longinquo obsidemur, et haeretici ex more grassantur. Itaque tempus admonuit adversus nostrates bestiolas (promptam) mederi theriacam stylo temperare; qui legeris, biberis. Non amarum potio. Si eloquia Domini dulcia super mella et favos, inde pigmenta sunt; si lacte et melle promissio Dei manat, hoc sapiunt quae illuc faciunt. Vae autem qui dulce in amarum, et lumen in tenebras convertunt. Perinde enim et qui martyriis refragantur, salutem perditionem interpretantes, tam dulce in amarum, quam lucem in tenebras reformant, atque ita miserrimam hanc vitam illi beatissimae praevertendo, tam amarum pro dulci, quam tenebras pro luce supponunt.
pass_a_gloss: Great evil from small thing scorpio earth suppurates: as many poisons, as many kinds; as many destructions, as many species; as many pains, as many colors, Nicander writes and depicts: and yet one gesture of violence of all to harm from the tail; which tail will be, whatever from the last part of the body is propagated, and strikes. Therefore that series of nodes of scorpios, a poisonous little vein inside, rising with curved impulse, holds a hooked point at the top of the torment with reason; whence also a war machine, with a throwing engine, is named from scorpio. That point, and also a pipe, with open thinness into the wound and the poison, with which it strikes and pours out. Familiar time of danger is summer; with the south wind and the African wind it rages. In remedies many natural things; also magic binds something, medicine with iron and cup occurs. For some also will drink beforehand, hastening protection; but intercourse exhausts, and again they thirst. To us faith is a protection, if not also it itself is struck by diffidence of signing at once and of adjuring, and of urging the heel of the beast: in this manner finally also to gentiles we often come to aid; gifted by God with that power, which the Apostle consecrated, when he despised the bite of a viper. What therefore does this style promise, if faith from its own is safe? So that also in other things from its own it may be safe, when it suffers its own scorpios. Bitter mediocrity is also to these, and varied kind, and they are armed in one way, and they are prepared at a certain time, and not otherwise than with ardor. This among Christians is persecution. When therefore faith is boiling, and the Church is being burned from the figure of a ruby, then the Gnostics burst forth, then the Valentinians break out, then all the refractors of martyrs boil over, being hot also to offend, to strike, to kill. For what they know many simple and unskilled, then weak, most indeed in the wind, and if it pleases, Christians, never more to be approached they perceive, than when the fear of the soul has loosened the approach; especially when some atrocity has crowned the faith of martyrs. And so at first drawing still the tail from the affections they apply, or as if into a vacuum they flagellate. Is this to be suffered by innocent men? So that you might think a brother, or one of the better gentiles? Is a sect that bothers no one to be treated thus? Then they drive men to perish without cause. For to perish, and without cause, is the first piercing. From then on they strike. But simple souls do not know what, how, it is written, where, and when, and before whom it is to be confessed, unless that not that simplicity, but vanity, indeed madness, is to die for God. And: Who will save me, if he who ought to save me kills? Christ died once for us, was killed once so that we might not be killed. If he demands a turn, now also he expects salvation from my death? Or does God demand the blood of men of the world, especially if he refuses that of bulls and goats? Certainly he prefers the repentance of a sinner to death. And how does he not desire the death of sins? These things, and if there are any other poisons of heretics, what do they not fix either in a scruple or in destruction? Or in bile, if not in death? But you, if faith is watchful, there the scorpio is struck with a sole, anathema having been applied, and the dying one is left in his own sleep. Moreover, if the wound has been satiated, it announces the poison, and hastens into the viscera; at once all the former senses are turned back, the blood of the soul grows cold, the spirit of the flesh is consumed, nausea at the name increases. Now also the mind itself seeks what it may vomit. And so once weakness which has been struck, wounded faith either into heresy or into the world expires. And now the present things are the middle ardor, the dog-star of persecution itself: from the cynocephalus itself. Others fire, others sword, others beasts have tested Christians. Others in prison, having tasted martyrdom with rods and nails, are hungry. We ourselves, like hares, a destined hunt, are besieged from afar, and heretics, as is their custom, prowl. And so the time has warned to prepare a remedy against our beasts; to temper a therapeutic writing; you who will read, will drink. The drink is not bitter. If the words of the Lord are sweeter than honey and honeycombs, from there are the seasonings; if the promise of God flows with milk and honey, these things have a taste that leads there. Woe however to those who convert sweet into bitter, and light into darkness. For just as those who resist martyrdom, interpreting salvation as perdition, so they reform sweet into bitter, and light into darkness, and thus they pervert this most wretched life, preferring the most blessed, so they substitute bitter for sweet, and darkness for light.

choices.english: from the figure of a ruby

pass_b_english: The earth breeds a massive evil from a tiny thing: the scorpion. Nicander writes and paints it— as many poisons as kinds, as many destructions as species, as many pains as colors. Yet for all that variety, a single gesture of violence does the harm: the strike of the tail. That tail is whatever extends from the body's rear, and it lashes out. So the scorpion's segmented tail, a poisonous vein inside, rises on a curved impulse and locks a hooked barb at the summit of its torment mechanism; hence a siege engine, its projectile springing from a drawn-back position, takes its name from the scorpion. That barb is also a duct, its open fineness channeling wound and venom; with it the creature strikes and injects. Summer is the familiar season of danger; the south wind and the African wind hoist its savagery. Remedies abound in nature; magic also binds something, and medicine meets the crisis with iron and cup. Some even drink beforehand, rushing protection; but intercourse exhausts the antidote, and they thirst again.

For us, faith is the shield— if it is not itself struck by the hesitation to sign, to adjure, to drive the beast's heel at once. In this way, finally, we often come to the aid of gentiles as well, endowed by God with the power the Apostle consecrated when he despised a viper's bite. So what does this pen promise, if faith is safe on its own account? That it may be safe on its own account in other matters too, when it endures its own scorpions. A bitter mediocrity belongs to these as well: varied kind, armed in one way, deployed at a set time, and driven by nothing but ardor. This, among Christians, is persecution.

When faith boils and the Church burns from the figure of the ruby, then the Gnostics burst out, the Valentinians break forth, and all the refusers of martyrdom boil over, hot themselves to offend, to stab, to kill. They know well that many are simple and unskilled, then weak, most indeed in the wind, and if it pleases, Christians— never do they perceive them more approachable than when fear of the soul has loosened the approach; especially when some atrocity has crowned the martyrs' faith. So at first, still drawing the tail from the affections, they apply it, or lash out as into a vacuum. Are innocent men to suffer this? So that you might take him for a brother, or one of the better gentiles? Is a sect that harms no one to be treated thus? Then they drive men to perish without cause. For to perish, and without cause, is the first piercing. From then on they kill.

But simple souls do not know what, how, where, when, or before whom it is written that confession must be made— unless it is not that simplicity, but vanity, indeed madness, to die for God. And: Who will save me, if the one who ought to save me kills? Christ died once for us, was killed once so that we might not be killed. If he demands a turn, does he now expect salvation from my death? Or does God demand the blood of the world's men, especially since he refuses that of bulls and goats? Certainly he prefers a sinner's repentance to death. And how does he not desire the death of sins? These poisons of the heretics, and any others— what do they not fix, whether in a scruple or in destruction? Or in bile, if not in death?

But you, if faith keeps watch, there strike the scorpion with a sandal, anathema applied, and leave the dying thing in its own sleep. Yet if the wound has had its fill, the venom announces itself and rushes to the vitals; at once all former senses grow numb, the soul's blood chills, the flesh's spirit goes cold, nausea at the Name swells. Even the mind now seeks something to vomit. And so, once struck, the weakness expires— wounded faith breathing its last either into heresy or into the world.

And now the present reality is the midday heat, the very dog-star of persecution: from the dog-headed one himself. Fire has tested some Christians, sword others, beasts others. Others in prison, having tasted martyrdom with rods and nails, hunger for it still. We ourselves, like hares marked for the hunt, are besieged from afar, and heretics prowl as is their custom. So the time has warned us to prepare a remedy against our little beasts: to compound a therapeutic writing with the pen; you who read, will drink. The draught is not bitter. If the Lord's words are sweeter than honey and comb, the seasonings come from there; if God's promise flows with milk and honey, these words taste the way that leads there. Woe to those who turn sweet to bitter and light to darkness. For just as those who resist martyrdom, interpreting salvation as perdition, turn sweet to bitter and light to darkness, so they pervert this most wretched life by preferring the most blessed one— substituting bitter for sweet, darkness for light.
